hypothesis: P1's function.zip ships no usable Python bytecode: 149 .pyc whose source-mtime headers do not match the 2026-01-01 stamp the build gives every .py, and no .pyc at all for most modules. /var/task is read-only, so every cold start (and every SnapStart snapshot init) compiles every imported module from source and cannot cache it. Shipping complete unchecked-hash bytecode cuts the cold `imports` phase, and therefore Init Duration and the start of the background model load, with no change to answers, warm inference or restore.

conclusion: Complete unchecked-hash bytecode halves the cold imports phase on every CPU part Lambda gave us (CPU part 0xd40 as read from /proc/cpuinfo, n=49/52: 0.719 -> 0.346 s, delta -0.373 s, 95% CI [-0.380, -0.367]; 0xd0c and 0xd4f the same direction in every shared round/part cell; all 12 shared cells below 0, with 5 sparse unmatched cells reported separately) and Init Duration by -0.380 s on 0xd40. Mechanism confirmed in-function: ctl recompiles all 153-157 task-root modules from source in every environment (0 usable .pyc), pyc recompiles 1 (the e6_entry wrapper itself). The cold first request does NOT improve: on 0xd40 first_request_total delta -0.012 s, CI [-0.098, +0.079]. On 0xd0c (n=5/3 only) it is -0.685 s, CI [-1.168, -0.322]; on 0xd4f (n=6/5) +0.047 s, CI [-0.271, +0.250]. That is no consistent improvement across parts. The reason: the on-demand load runs in PR #77's background thread and the request waits for the ~25 s S3 download, which starts after imports either way; the saved ~0.37 s goes back into wait_for_load (weight_download on pyc +0.30 s, CI [+0.258, +0.383], a download that starts earlier and ends at the same time: import_total + weight_download p50 25.75 vs 25.68 s). Billed cold duration is unchanged (REPORT Billed Duration includes Init; the Init saved is spent waiting for the load inside Duration). SnapStart snapshot init imports also halve (0.665 -> 0.332 s, n=6/6), but that is publish time, not restore latency: restore first request total delta -0.045 s, CI [-0.097, +0.014] (0xd40 only). Warm inference unchanged (+0.0077 s, CI [-0.0100, +0.0251]). Answers: 420/420 pyc answers bit-identical to ctl for the same request and CPU part, and every answer P1's reference covers is bit-identical to it. Recommendation: adopt (no cost, +7 MB zip / +19 MB unzipped of the 250 MB limit, ~9 MB less peak memory) as hygiene; it pays off only where imports are on the request path, i.e. after a change that overlaps or removes the download (E4, E5, E9 or a combined ladder rung), so R should re-measure it there rather than credit it to the current baseline.

host_variability.method: Within each observed CPU part, compare arm medians in each round. Arms are sequential waves whose first position alternates by round; this is alternation, not within-round interleaving. Missing-arm cells and rows without CPU identity are listed but never treated as comparable strata.
